ko:
오늘은 안드레이 카파시와
이야기를 나눠보겠습니다.
en: Today I'm speaking with Andrej Karpathy.

ko:
안드레이, 왜 이걸
'에이전트의 해'가 아니라
en: Andrej, why do you say that this will be the decade of agents and not the year of agents?

ko:
'에이전트의 10년'이라고
하시는 건가요?
en: Andrej, why do you say that this will be the decade of agents and not the year of agents?

ko:
먼저, 이 자리에 초대해
주셔서 감사합니다.
en: First of all, thank you for having me here.

ko: 이렇게 함께하게 되어 기쁘네요.
en: I'm excited to be here.

ko: 방금 말씀하신 '에이전트의 10년'이라는
en: The quote you've just mentioned, "It's the decade of agents," is actually a reaction to a pre-existing quote.

ko:
표현은 사실 기존에 있던
말에 대한 반응이에요.
en: The quote you've just mentioned, "It's the decade of agents," is actually a reaction to a pre-existing quote.

ko:
누가 한 말인지는 정확히
모르겠지만, LLM이 앞으로 어떻게
en: I'm not actually sure who said this but they were alluding to this being the year of agents with respect to LLMs and how they were going to evolve.

ko:
진화할지를 두고 '에이전트의
해'라고 암시한 거였어요.
en: I'm not actually sure who said this but they were alluding to this being the year of agents with respect to LLMs and how they were going to evolve.

ko:
그 말에 좀 자극을
받았는데, 업계에 과도한
en: I was triggered by that because there's some over-prediction going on in the industry.

ko: 예측이 퍼져 있다고 느꼈기 때문이에요.
en: I was triggered by that because there's some over-prediction going on in the industry.

ko:
제 생각엔 이건
'에이전트의 10년'이라고
en: In my mind, this is more accurately described as the decade of agents.

ko: 하는 게 더 정확한 표현인 것 같아요.
en: In my mind, this is more accurately described as the decade of agents.

ko:
지금도 아주 초기 단계의
에이전트들, 그러니까 Claude나
en: We have some very early agents that are extremely impressive and that I use daily—Claude and Codex and so on—but I still feel there's so much work to be done.

ko:
Codex 같은 것들이 정말
인상적이고 저도 매일 쓰고
en: We have some very early agents that are extremely impressive and that I use daily—Claude and Codex and so on—but I still feel there's so much work to be done.

ko:
있지만, 아직 해야 할 일이
정말 많다고 느껴져요.
en: We have some very early agents that are extremely impressive and that I use daily—Claude and Codex and so on—but I still feel there's so much work to be done.

ko:
그래서 제 반응은,
우리가 이 녀석들과 앞으로
en: My reaction is we'll be working with these things for a decade.

ko: 10년은 함께 일하게 될 거라는 거예요.
en: My reaction is we'll be working with these things for a decade.

ko:
계속 더 좋아질 거고, 정말
멋진 일이 될 거예요.
en: They're going to get better, and it's going to be wonderful.

ko:
저는 그냥 그 말이 함축하는
시간축에 반응한 거였어요.
en: I was just reacting to the timelines of the implication.

ko:
그럼 10년이 걸릴 거라고
보시는 건 구체적으로 뭔가요?
en: What do you think will take a decade to accomplish?

ko: 병목은 뭔가요?
en: What are the bottlenecks?

ko: 실제로 작동하게 만드는 것, 그 자체요.
en: Actually making it work.

ko:
에이전트라고 할 때, 그러니까
랩들이 염두에 둔 것,
en: When you're talking about an agent, or what the labs have in mind and maybe what I have in mind as well, you should think of it almost like an employee or an intern that you would hire to work with you.

ko:
그리고 아마 저도 마찬가지인데,
이건 거의 같이 일할
en: When you're talking about an agent, or what the labs have in mind and maybe what I have in mind as well, you should think of it almost like an employee or an intern that you would hire to work with you.

ko:
직원이나 인턴을 채용하는
것처럼 생각하시면 돼요.
en: When you're talking about an agent, or what the labs have in mind and maybe what I have in mind as well, you should think of it almost like an employee or an intern that you would hire to work with you.

ko:
예를 들어 여기서도 몇몇
직원분들과 함께 일하시잖아요.
en: For example, you work with some employees here.

ko:
그 일을 Claude나
Codex 같은 에이전트가
en: When would you prefer to have an agent like Claude or Codex do that work?

ko:
대신 하게 하고 싶어지는
건 언제쯤일까요?
en: When would you prefer to have an agent like Claude or Codex do that work?

ko: 지금은 당연히 못 하죠.
en: Currently, of course they can't.

ko: 그게 가능해지려면 뭐가 필요할까요?
en: What would it take for them to be able to do that?

ko: 지금은 왜 그렇게 안 하시는 거죠?
en: Why don't you do it today?

ko:
지금 안 하시는 이유는, 그냥 아직
제대로 작동을 안 하기 때문이에요.
en: The reason you don't do it today is because they just don't work.

ko:
지능이 충분치 않고,
멀티모달 능력도 부족하고,
en: They don't have enough intelligence, they're not multimodal enough, they can't do computer use and all this stuff.

ko:
컴퓨터 사용 같은 것도
제대로 못 하고요.
en: They don't have enough intelligence, they're not multimodal enough, they can't do computer use and all this stuff.

ko:
아까 말씀하신 것들 중에도
못 하는 게 많고요.
en: They don't do a lot of the things you've alluded to earlier.

ko: 연속 학습 능력도 없어요.
en: They don't have continual learning.

ko:
그냥 뭔가 말해준다고 그걸
기억하는 게 아니에요.
en: You can't just tell them something and they'll remember it.

ko:
인지적으로 결핍돼 있어서,
그냥 잘 안 되는 거예요.
en: They're cognitively lacking and it's just not working.

ko:
이 모든 문제를 다 해결하는 데
대략 10년 정도 걸릴 거예요.
en: It will take about a decade to work through all of those issues.

ko: 흥미롭네요.
en: Interesting.

ko:
전문 팟캐스터로서, 그리고
AI를 멀리서 지켜보는 사람으로서
en: As a professional podcaster and a viewer of AI from afar, it's easy for me to identify what's lacking: continual learning is lacking, or multimodality is lacking.

ko:
저도 뭐가 부족한지는 쉽게
짚을 수 있어요 — 연속
en: As a professional podcaster and a viewer of AI from afar, it's easy for me to identify what's lacking: continual learning is lacking, or multimodality is lacking.

ko:
학습이 부족하다, 멀티모달리티가
부족하다, 이런 식으로요.
en: As a professional podcaster and a viewer of AI from afar, it's easy for me to identify what's lacking: continual learning is lacking, or multimodality is lacking.

ko:
하지만 거기에 정확히 언제까지라고
못 박을 좋은 방법은 딱히 없어요.
en: But I don't really have a good way of trying to put a timeline on it.

ko:
누가 연속 학습이 얼마나 걸릴지
물으면, 이게 5년짜리 프로젝트인지
en: If somebody asks how long continual learning will take, I have no prior about whether this is a project that should take 5 years, 10 years, or 50 years.

ko:
10년짜리인지 50년짜리인지에
대한 사전 감이 전혀 없어요.
en: If somebody asks how long continual learning will take, I have no prior about whether this is a project that should take 5 years, 10 years, or 50 years.

ko: 왜 10년인가요?
en: Why a decade?

ko: 왜 1년은 아닌가요?
en: Why not one year?

ko: 왜 50년은 아닌가요?
en: Why not 50 years?

ko:
여기서부터는 제 나름의 직관이
좀 들어가는데요, 이 분야에서의
en: This is where you get into a bit of my own intuition, and doing a bit of an extrapolation with respect to my own experience in the field.

ko:
제 경험을 바탕으로 어느
정도 외삽을 해보는 거예요.
en: This is where you get into a bit of my own intuition, and doing a bit of an extrapolation with respect to my own experience in the field.

ko:
저는 거의 20년
가까이 AI를 해왔어요.
en: I've been in AI for almost two decades.

ko: 15년 정도예요, 그렇게 길지는 않고요.
en: It's going to be 15 years or so, not that long.

ko:
여기 리처드 서튼도 나오셨었는데,
그분은 훨씬 더 오래 계셨죠.
en: You had Richard Sutton here, who was around for much longer.

ko:
그래도 저는 사람들이
예측을 하고 그게 어떻게
en: I do have about 15 years of experience of people making predictions, of seeing how they turned out.

ko:
됐는지 지켜본 경험이
15년 정도는 있어요.
en: I do have about 15 years of experience of people making predictions, of seeing how they turned out.

ko:
또 저는 한동안 업계에
있었고, 연구 쪽에도
en: Also I was in the industry for a while, I was in research, and I've worked in the industry for a while.

ko:
있었고, 업계에서
한동안 일하기도 했어요.
en: Also I was in the industry for a while, I was in research, and I've worked in the industry for a while.

ko: 거기서 남은 전반적인 직관이 있어요.
en: I have a general intuition that I have left from that.

ko:
이 문제들이 다룰 수
있고 극복 가능한 것
en: I feel like the problems are tractable, they're surmountable, but they're still difficult.

ko:
같지만, 그래도 여전히
어렵다는 느낌이에요.
en: I feel like the problems are tractable, they're surmountable, but they're still difficult.

ko:
그냥 평균을 내보면, 제겐
대략 10년 정도로 느껴져요.
en: If I just average it out, it just feels like a decade to me.

ko: 이거 꽤 흥미롭네요.
en: This is quite interesting.

ko:
역사 자체뿐 아니라, 여러
돌파구의 순간마다 그 자리에 있던
en: I want to hear not only the history, but what people in the room felt was about to happen at various different breakthrough moments.

ko:
사람들이 앞으로 무슨 일이 일어날
거라고 느꼈는지도 듣고 싶어요.
en: I want to hear not only the history, but what people in the room felt was about to happen at various different breakthrough moments.

ko: 그 느낌들이 어떤 식으로 지나치게
en: What were the ways in which their feelings were either overly pessimistic or overly optimistic?

ko: 비관적이었거나, 지나치게 낙관적이었나요?
en: What were the ways in which their feelings were either overly pessimistic or overly optimistic?

ko: 하나씩 차례로 짚어볼까요?
en: Should we just go through each of them one by one?

ko:
그건 엄청나게 큰
질문이에요, 15년 동안
en: That's a giant question because you're talking about 15 years of stuff that happened.

ko: 일어난 일들을 다 얘기하는 거니까요.
en: That's a giant question because you're talking about 15 years of stuff that happened.

ko:
AI가 정말 멋진 이유는, 분야
전체가 갑자기 완전히 다른 모습으로
en: AI is so wonderful because there have been a number of seismic shifts where the entire field has suddenly looked a different way.

ko:
보이게 되는 지각변동 같은 순간들이
여러 번 있었기 때문이에요.
en: AI is so wonderful because there have been a number of seismic shifts where the entire field has suddenly looked a different way.

ko:
저도 아마 그런 걸 두세
번은 겪은 것 같아요.
en: I've maybe lived through two or three of those.

ko:
앞으로도 계속 있을 거라고 봐요,
놀라울 정도로 규칙적으로 찾아오거든요.
en: I still think there will continue to be some because they come with almost surprising regularity.

ko:
제 경력이 시작될 때, 딥러닝을
시작했을 때, 딥러닝에
en: When my career began, when I started to work on deep learning, when I became interested in deep learning, this was by chance of being right next to Geoff Hinton at the University of Toronto.

ko:
관심을 갖게 됐을 때, 그건
우연히 토론토 대학교에서
en: When my career began, when I started to work on deep learning, when I became interested in deep learning, this was by chance of being right next to Geoff Hinton at the University of Toronto.

ko:
제프리 힌튼 바로 옆에
있었기 때문이었어요.
en: When my career began, when I started to work on deep learning, when I became interested in deep learning, this was by chance of being right next to Geoff Hinton at the University of Toronto.

ko:
제프리 힌튼은 물론 AI의
대부 같은 인물이죠.
en: Geoff Hinton, of course, is the godfather figure of AI.

ko:
그는 온갖 신경망들을
훈련시키고 있었어요.
en: He was training all these neural networks.

ko:
저는 그게 정말 놀랍고
흥미롭다고 생각했어요.
en: I thought it was incredible and interesting.

ko:
당시 AI 업계 사람들 대부분이
하던 주된 일과는 거리가 멀었죠.
en: This was not the main thing that everyone in AI was doing by far.

ko: 그냥 곁가지의 작은 틈새 주제였어요.
en: This was a niche little subject on the side.

ko: 그게 아마 AlexNet과 함께 찾아온
en: That's maybe the first dramatic seismic shift that came with the AlexNet and so on.

ko: 첫 번째 극적인 지각변동이었을 거예요.
en: That's maybe the first dramatic seismic shift that came with the AlexNet and so on.

ko:
AlexNet이 다들 방향을 바꾸게
했고, 다들 신경망을 훈련시키기
en: AlexNet reoriented everyone, and everyone started to train neural networks, but it was still very per-task, per specific task.

ko:
시작했지만, 그래도 여전히 과제별로,
특정 과제 하나하나에 맞춘 거였어요.
en: AlexNet reoriented everyone, and everyone started to train neural networks, but it was still very per-task, per specific task.

ko:
예를 들면 이미지 분류기 하나, 신경망
기계번역기 하나, 그런 식이었죠.
en: Maybe I have an image classifier or I have a neural machine translator or something like that.

ko:
사람들은 아주 서서히 에이전트에
관심을 갖기 시작했어요.
en: People became very slowly interested in agents.

ko:
"좋아, 시각피질 부분은 이제
체크했다 치고, 뇌의 나머지
en: People started to think, "Okay, maybe we have a check mark next to the visual cortex or something like that, but what about the other parts of the brain, and how can we get a full agent or a full entity that can interact in the world?"

ko:
부분들은? 세상과 상호작용할
수 있는 온전한 에이전트,
en: People started to think, "Okay, maybe we have a check mark next to the visual cortex or something like that, but what about the other parts of the brain, and how can we get a full agent or a full entity that can interact in the world?"

ko:
온전한 개체는 어떻게 얻지?"
라고 생각하기 시작한 거죠.
en: People started to think, "Okay, maybe we have a check mark next to the visual cortex or something like that, but what about the other parts of the brain, and how can we get a full agent or a full entity that can interact in the world?"

ko:
제 생각엔 2013년쯤 있었던 아타리
심층강화학습으로의 전환이 그 초기
en: The Atari deep reinforcement learning shift in 2013 or so was part of that early effort of agents, in my mind, because it was an attempt to try to get agents that not just perceive the world, but also take actions and interact and get rewards from environments.

ko:
에이전트 노력의 일부였어요, 세상을
지각할 뿐 아니라 행동을 취하고
en: The Atari deep reinforcement learning shift in 2013 or so was part of that early effort of agents, in my mind, because it was an attempt to try to get agents that not just perceive the world, but also take actions and interact and get rewards from environments.

ko:
상호작용하고 환경에서 보상을 받는
에이전트를 만들려는 시도였으니까요.
en: The Atari deep reinforcement learning shift in 2013 or so was part of that early effort of agents, in my mind, because it was an attempt to try to get agents that not just perceive the world, but also take actions and interact and get rewards from environments.

ko: 당시엔 그게 아타리 게임이었죠.
en: At the time, this was Atari games.

ko: 저는 그게 헛발질이었다고 생각해요.
en: I feel that was a misstep.

ko:
제가 몸담았던 초기 OpenAI조차
받아들였던 헛발질이었어요, 그 시절
en: It was a misstep that even the early OpenAI that I was a part of adopted because at that time, the zeitgeist was reinforcement learning environments, games, game playing, beat games, get lots of different types of games, and OpenAI was doing a lot of that.

ko:
시대정신이 강화학습 환경, 게임, 게임
플레이, 게임 깨기, 온갖 종류의
en: It was a misstep that even the early OpenAI that I was a part of adopted because at that time, the zeitgeist was reinforcement learning environments, games, game playing, beat games, get lots of different types of games, and OpenAI was doing a lot of that.

ko:
게임을 확보하는 거였고, OpenAI도
그런 걸 많이 하고 있었거든요.
en: It was a misstep that even the early OpenAI that I was a part of adopted because at that time, the zeitgeist was reinforcement learning environments, games, game playing, beat games, get lots of different types of games, and OpenAI was doing a lot of that.

ko:
그게 AI의 또 다른 두드러진
부분이었는데, 한 2,
en: That was another prominent part of AI where maybe for two or three or four years, everyone was doing reinforcement learning on games.

ko:
3, 4년 동안은 다들 게임에
강화학습을 하고 있었어요.
en: That was another prominent part of AI where maybe for two or three or four years, everyone was doing reinforcement learning on games.

ko: 그것도 다 조금은 헛발질이었죠.
en: That was all a bit of a misstep.

ko:
제가 OpenAI에서
하려던 건... 저는 늘
en: What I was trying to do at OpenAI is I was always a bit suspicious of games as being this thing that would lead to AGI.

ko:
게임이 AGI로 이어질
거라는 데 좀 회의적이었어요.
en: What I was trying to do at OpenAI is I was always a bit suspicious of games as being this thing that would lead to AGI.

ko:
왜냐하면 제 생각엔,
회계사 같은 것, 실제
en: Because in my mind, you want something like an accountant or something that's interacting with the real world.

ko:
세상과 상호작용하는 뭔가가
필요하다고 봤거든요.
en: Because in my mind, you want something like an accountant or something that's interacting with the real world.

ko:
게임이 어떻게 그런 걸로 이어지는지
도무지 알 수가 없었어요.
en: I just didn't see how games add up to it.

ko:
예를 들어 제가 OpenAI에서
했던 프로젝트는
en: My project at OpenAI, for example, was within the scope of the Universe project, on an agent that was using keyboard and mouse to operate web pages.

ko:
유니버스(Universe)
프로젝트 범위 안에서, 키보드와
en: My project at OpenAI, for example, was within the scope of the Universe project, on an agent that was using keyboard and mouse to operate web pages.

ko:
마우스로 웹페이지를 조작하는
에이전트에 관한 거였어요.
en: My project at OpenAI, for example, was within the scope of the Universe project, on an agent that was using keyboard and mouse to operate web pages.

ko:
저는 정말로 실제 디지털
세상과 상호작용하면서

조용히요—개별 예시 하나만

그런데 그걸 열 번 물어보면, 전부

하는 말은 아니거든요, 아직

ko: 흥미로운 질문이네요.
en: That's an interesting question.

ko:
지금 영상의학과에서 그런 일이
일어나고 있다고는 생각하지 않아요.
en: I don't think we're currently seeing that with radiology.

ko:
영상의학과는 좋은
예시가 아닌 것 같아요.
en: I think radiology is not a good example.

ko:
제프리 힌튼이 왜 하필 영상의학과를
콕 집었는지 모르겠어요.
en: I don't know why Geoff Hinton picked on radiology because I think it's an extremely messy, complicated profession.

ko:
굉장히 지저분하고 복잡한
직종이라고 생각하거든요.
en: I don't know why Geoff Hinton picked on radiology because I think it's an extremely messy, complicated profession.

ko:
저는 오히려 오늘날 콜센터
직원들에게 무슨 일이 일어나고
en: I would be a lot more interested in what's happening with call center employees today, for example, because I would expect a lot of the rote stuff to be automatable today.

ko:
있는지가 훨씬 궁금해요.
예를 들면 반복적인 업무는
en: I would be a lot more interested in what's happening with call center employees today, for example, because I would expect a lot of the rote stuff to be automatable today.

ko:
지금도 상당히 자동화
가능할 거라고 예상하거든요.
en: I would be a lot more interested in what's happening with call center employees today, for example, because I would expect a lot of the rote stuff to be automatable today.

ko:
제가 직접 접근할 수 있는 데이터는
아니지만, 콜센터 직원들한테
en: I don't have first-level access to it but I would be looking for trends of what's happening with the call center employees.

ko:
무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 그
추세를 계속 지켜보고 싶어요.
en: I don't have first-level access to it but I would be looking for trends of what's happening with the call center employees.

ko:
제가 예상하는 것 중 하나는,
어쩌면 AI로 교체하더라도
en: Some of the things I would also expect is that maybe they are swapping in AI, but then I would still wait for a year or two because I would potentially expect them to pull back and rehire some of the people.

ko:
저는 여전히 1~2년 정도는
지켜볼 거라는 거예요. 다시
en: Some of the things I would also expect is that maybe they are swapping in AI, but then I would still wait for a year or two because I would potentially expect them to pull back and rehire some of the people.

ko:
발을 빼고 사람 일부를 재고용할
가능성이 있다고 보거든요.
en: Some of the things I would also expect is that maybe they are swapping in AI, but then I would still wait for a year or two because I would potentially expect them to pull back and rehire some of the people.

ko:
실제로 AI를 도입한 회사들
전반에서 이미 그런 일이
en: There's been evidence that that's already been happening generally in companies that have been adopting AI, which I think is quite surprising.

ko:
일어나고 있다는 증거가 있는데,
이건 꽤 놀랍다고 생각해요.
en: There's been evidence that that's already been happening generally in companies that have been adopting AI, which I think is quite surprising.

ko: 저도 정말 놀랍다고 느낀 게 있었어요.
en: I also found what was really surprising.

ko: AGI 말이에요, 그렇죠?
en: AGI, right?

ko: 모든 걸 다 할 수 있는 존재요.
en: A thing which would do everything.

ko:
육체노동은 빼더라도, 모든
지식노동은 할 수 있어야 하잖아요.
en: We'll take out physical work, but it should be able to do all knowledge work.

ko:
순진하게 예상했던 진행
방식은, 컨설턴트가 하는
en: What you would have naively anticipated is that the way this progression would happen is that you take a little task that a consultant is doing, you take that out of the bucket.

ko:
작은 업무 하나를 그
업무 바구니에서 빼내고,
en: What you would have naively anticipated is that the way this progression would happen is that you take a little task that a consultant is doing, you take that out of the bucket.

ko:
회계사가 하는 작은 업무
하나를 그 바구니에서 빼내고,
en: You take a little task that an accountant is doing, you take that out of the bucket.

ko:
이런 식으로 모든 지식노동에
걸쳐 진행되는 거였어요.
en: Then you're just doing this across all knowledge work.

ko:
그런데 만약 우리가 지금
패러다임으로 AGI로 가는 길 위에
en: But instead, if we do believe we're on the path of AGI with the current paradigm, the progression is very much not like that.

ko:
있다고 믿는다면, 실제 진행
양상은 전혀 그렇지 않아요.
en: But instead, if we do believe we're on the path of AGI with the current paradigm, the progression is very much not like that.

ko:
컨설턴트나 회계사가 엄청난 생산성
향상을 얻고 있는 것 같지는 않아요.
en: It does not seem like consultants and accountants are getting huge productivity improvements.

ko: 오히려 프로그래머들의 업무가 점점 더
en: It's very much like programmers are getting more and more chiseled away at their work.

ko: 깎여 나가고 있는 모습에 훨씬 가까워요.
en: It's very much like programmers are getting more and more chiseled away at their work.

ko:
이 회사들의 매출을 보면, 구글
같은 데와 비슷한 일반 챗
en: If you look at the revenues of these companies, discounting normal chat revenue—which is similar to Google or something—just looking at API revenues, it's dominated by coding.

ko:
매출은 제외하고 API 매출만
봐도, 코딩이 압도적이에요.
en: If you look at the revenues of these companies, discounting normal chat revenue—which is similar to Google or something—just looking at API revenues, it's dominated by coding.

ko:
그러니까 '범용적'이어야 하는,
어떤 지식노동이든 할 수 있어야
en: So this thing which is "general", which should be able to do any knowledge work, is just overwhelmingly doing only coding.

ko:
하는 이 존재가 사실상 압도적으로
코딩만 하고 있는 거예요.
en: So this thing which is "general", which should be able to do any knowledge work, is just overwhelmingly doing only coding.

ko:
AGI가 이런 식으로 쓰일
거라고 예상했던 모습은 아니죠.
en: It's a surprising way that you would expect the AGI to be deployed.

ko: 여기 흥미로운 지점이 있어요.
en: There's an interesting point here.

ko:
저는 코딩이 이런 LLM들과 에이전트들에게
완벽한 첫 단추라고 생각해요.
en: I do believe coding is the perfect first thing for these LLMs and agents.

ko:
왜냐하면 코딩은 원래부터 근본적으로
텍스트를 중심으로 돌아가거든요.
en: That’s because coding has always fundamentally worked around text.

ko:
컴퓨터 터미널도 텍스트고, 모든
게 텍스트를 기반으로 하죠.
en: It's computer terminals and text, and everything is based around text.

ko:
LLM은 인터넷 데이터로 학습되다
보니 텍스트를 좋아해요.
en: LLMs, the way they're trained on the Internet, love text.

ko:
완벽한 텍스트 처리기인 데다, 이미
그런 데이터가 세상에 넘쳐나죠.
en: They're perfect text processors, and there's all this data out there.

ko: 완벽하게 맞아떨어지는 조합인 거예요.
en: It's a perfect fit.

ko:
코드와 텍스트를 다루기 위한
인프라도 이미 많이 갖춰져 있고요.
en: We also have a lot of infrastructure pre-built for handling code and text.

ko:
예를 들어 Visual Studio
Code나 여러분이 쓰는 IDE가
en: For example, we have Visual Studio Code or your favorite IDE showing you code, and an agent can plug into that.

ko:
코드를 보여주는데, 에이전트는
거기에 바로 연결할 수 있어요.
en: For example, we have Visual Studio Code or your favorite IDE showing you code, and an agent can plug into that.

ko:
에이전트가 어떤 변경을
했다면, 코드베이스의 차이를
en: If an agent has a diff where it made some change, we suddenly have all this code already that shows all the differences to a code base using a diff.

ko:
보여주는 diff라는 게
이미 다 마련돼 있는 거죠.
en: If an agent has a diff where it made some change, we suddenly have all this code already that shows all the differences to a code base using a diff.

ko:
코드를 위한 인프라는 이미 상당 부분
미리 지어놓은 것과 마찬가지예요.
en: It's almost like we've pre-built a lot of the infrastructure for code.

ko:
이런 걸 전혀 누리지 못하는
것들과 비교해보면 다르죠.
en: Contrast that with some of the things that don't enjoy that at all.

ko: 예를 들어 코딩이 아니라 슬라이드를 위한

ko: 자동화를 만들려는 사람들이 있어요.
en: As an example, there are people trying to build automation not for coding, but for slides.

ko: 슬라이드 만드는 회사를 하나 봤는데요.
en: I saw a company doing slides.

ko: 그게 훨씬, 훨씬 더 어려워요.
en: That's much, much harder.

ko:
훨씬 어려운 이유는 슬라이드가
텍스트가 아니기 때문이에요.
en: The reason it's much harder is because slides are not text.

ko: 슬라이드는 작은 그래픽들이 공간적으로
en: Slides are little graphics, they're arranged spatially, and there's a visual component to it.

ko: 배치된 거고, 시각적인 요소가 있죠.
en: Slides are little graphics, they're arranged spatially, and there's a visual component to it.

ko:
슬라이드에는 이렇게 미리
마련된 인프라가 없어요.
en: Slides don't have this pre-built infrastructure.

ko: 예를 들어 에이전트가 슬라이드를
en: For example, if an agent is to make a change to your slides, how does a thing show you the diff?

ko:
바꾼다면, 그 diff를
어떻게 보여주죠?
en: For example, if an agent is to make a change to your slides, how does a thing show you the diff?

ko: diff를 어떻게 확인하나요?
en: How do you see the diff?

ko:
슬라이드용 diff를 보여주는
건 아무것도 없어요.
en: There's nothing that shows diffs for slides.

ko: 누군가 만들어야 하는 거죠.
en: Someone has to build it.

ko:
이런 것들 중 일부는 지금의
AI, 그러니까 텍스트 처리기인
en: Some of these things are not amenable to AIs as they are, which are text processors, and code surprisingly is.

ko:
AI에 잘 맞지 않는데,
코딩은 의외로 딱 맞는 거예요.
en: Some of these things are not amenable to AIs as they are, which are text processors, and code surprisingly is.

ko: 그것만으로는 설명이 안 되는 것 같아요.
en: I’m not sure that alone explains it.

ko:
저는 개인적으로 순수하게
언어를 넣으면 언어가 나오는

ko:
영역—대본을 다시 쓴다거나,
대본을 바탕으로 클립을 만든다거나
en: I personally have tried to get LLMs to be useful in domains which are just pure language-in, language-out, like rewriting transcripts, coming up with clips based on transcripts.

ko:
하는 일—에서 LLM을 유용하게
쓰려고 시도해 봤어요.
en: I personally have tried to get LLMs to be useful in domains which are just pure language-in, language-out, like rewriting transcripts, coming up with clips based on transcripts.

ko:
제가 할 수 있는 걸 다 해본
건 아닐 가능성이 커요.
en: It's very plausible that I didn't do every single possible thing I could do.

ko:
컨텍스트에 좋은 예시들을
잔뜩 넣긴 했는데, 어쩌면
en: I put a bunch of good examples in context, but maybe I should have done some kind of fine-tuning.

ko:
파인튜닝 같은 걸 했어야
했는지도 모르겠어요.
en: I put a bunch of good examples in context, but maybe I should have done some kind of fine-tuning.

ko:
저희 둘 다 아는 친구 앤디
마투샥은, 모델이 간격 반복 카드를
en: Our mutual friend, Andy Matuschak, told me that he tried 50 billion things to try to get models to be good at writing spaced repetition prompts.

ko:
잘 만들게 하려고 500억
가지를 시도해봤다고 하더라고요.
en: Our mutual friend, Andy Matuschak, told me that he tried 50 billion things to try to get models to be good at writing spaced repetition prompts.

ko:
이것도 완전히 언어를 넣으면
언어가 나오는 작업이고,
en: Again, very much language-in, language-out tasks, the kind of thing that should be dead center in the repertoire of these LLMs.

ko:
LLM의 주특기 한복판에
있어야 할 일이죠.
en: Again, very much language-in, language-out tasks, the kind of thing that should be dead center in the repertoire of these LLMs.

ko:
그는 몇 개의 예시를 주는
인컨텍스트 러닝을 시도했어요.
en: He tried in-context learning with a few-shot examples.

ko:
지도 파인튜닝과
검색(retrieval)도 시도했고요.
en: He tried supervised fine-tuning and retrieval.

ko:
그런데도 자기 마음에 들게
카드를 만들게 할 수는 없었대요.
en: He could not get them to make cards to his satisfaction.

ko:
그래서 저는 언어를 출력하는
영역에서조차, 코딩을 제외하면 이

ko:
모델들에서 큰 경제적 가치를 뽑아내기가
굉장히 어렵다는 게 흥미로워요.
en: So I find it striking that even in language-out domains, it's very hard to get a lot of economic value out of these models separate from coding.

ko: 뭐가 원인인지 모르겠어요.
en: I don't know what explains it.

ko: 그건 말이 되네요.
en: That makes sense.

ko: 텍스트라고 다 쉽다는 얘기는 아니에요.
en: I'm not saying that anything text is trivial.

ko: 코드는 꽤 구조화되어 있다고 생각해요.
en: I do think that code is pretty structured.

ko:
텍스트는 훨씬 더 화려하고,
엔트로피가 훨씬 많다고 할까요.
en: Text is maybe a lot more flowery, and there's a lot more entropy in text, I would say.

ko: 달리 어떻게 표현해야 할지 모르겠네요.
en: I don't know how else to put it.

ko:
게다가 코드는 어려운 일이라,
아주 단순한 지식만으로도
en: Also code is hard, and so people feel quite empowered by LLMs, even from simple knowledge.

ko:
사람들이 LLM 덕분에 꽤
힘을 얻은 느낌을 받아요.
en: Also code is hard, and so people feel quite empowered by LLMs, even from simple knowledge.

ko:
아주 좋은 답을 갖고 있는
건 아닌 것 같아요.
en: I don't know that I have a very good answer.

ko:
물론 텍스트라서 훨씬,
훨씬 쉬워지긴 하지만,
en: Obviously, text makes it much, much easier, but it doesn't mean that all text is trivial.

ko:
그렇다고 모든 텍스트가
쉽다는 뜻은 아니에요.
en: Obviously, text makes it much, much easier, but it doesn't mean that all text is trivial.

ko: 초지능은 어떻게 생각하세요?
en: How do you think about superintelligence?

ko: 평범한 인간이나 인간 회사들과는 질적으로
en: Do you expect it to feel qualitatively different from normal humans or human companies?

ko: 다르게 느껴질 거라고 예상하시나요?
en: Do you expect it to feel qualitatively different from normal humans or human companies?

ko:
저는 그걸 사회 속 자동화의
진행 과정으로 봐요.
en: I see it as a progression of automation in society.

ko:
컴퓨팅의 흐름을 그대로
연장해보면, 많은 것들이
en: Extrapolating the trend of computing, there will be a gradual automation of a lot of things, and superintelligence will an extrapolation of that.

ko:
점진적으로 자동화될 거고,
초지능은 그 연장선일 뿐이에요.
en: Extrapolating the trend of computing, there will be a gradual automation of a lot of things, and superintelligence will an extrapolation of that.

ko:
시간이 지날수록 점점 더 자율적인
개체들이 늘어나서 디지털 작업의 상당
en: We expect more and more autonomous entities over time that are doing a lot of the digital work and then eventually even the physical work some amount of time later.

ko:
부분을 하고, 어느 정도 지나면 물리적인
작업까지 하게 될 거라고 봐요.
en: We expect more and more autonomous entities over time that are doing a lot of the digital work and then eventually even the physical work some amount of time later.

ko:
그러니까 대략 말하자면,
저는 그냥 자동화라고 봐요.
en: Basically I see it as just automation, roughly speaking.

ko:
하지만 자동화는 인간이 이미
할 수 있는 일들을 포함하고,
en: But automation includes the things humans can already do, and superintelligence implies things humans can’t do.

ko:
초지능은 인간이 할 수
없는 일들을 의미하잖아요.
en: But automation includes the things humans can already do, and superintelligence implies things humans can’t do.

ko:
근데 사람들이 하는 일 중 하나가
새로운 걸 발명하는 건데, 저는
en: But one of the things that people do is invent new things, which I would just put into the automation if that makes sense.

ko:
그것도 그냥 자동화에 넣을 것
같아요, 말이 되는지 모르겠지만요.
en: But one of the things that people do is invent new things, which I would just put into the automation if that makes sense.

ko:
그런데 좀 덜 추상적으로,
더 질적인 측면에서
en: But I guess, less abstractly and more qualitatively, do you expect something to feel like…

ko:
여쭤보면, 뭔가 이런
느낌일 거라고 예상하시나요…
en: But I guess, less abstractly and more qualitatively, do you expect something to feel like…

ko:
이 존재가 너무 빨리 생각하거나,
사본이 너무 많거나, 그
en: Because this thing can either think so fast, or has so many copies, or the copies can merge back into themselves, or is much smarter, any number of advantages an AI might have, will the civilization in which these AIs exist just feel qualitatively different from humans?

ko:
사본들이 다시 하나로 합쳐지거나,
훨씬 더 똑똑하거나 —
en: Because this thing can either think so fast, or has so many copies, or the copies can merge back into themselves, or is much smarter, any number of advantages an AI might have, will the civilization in which these AIs exist just feel qualitatively different from humans?

ko:
AI가 가질 수 있는 그 어떤
이점 때문이든, 그런 AI들이
en: Because this thing can either think so fast, or has so many copies, or the copies can merge back into themselves, or is much smarter, any number of advantages an AI might have, will the civilization in which these AIs exist just feel qualitatively different from humans?

ko:

거네요. 훨씬 더 강도

년간 그래왔듯 사람들이

예를 들어 귀족들이나 고대 그리스

인지적으로든 나름의 방식으로
번영하는 데 많은 시간을 썼어요.

저는 그 전망에 대해서는
꽤 괜찮다고 느껴요.

만약 이게 틀렸고 제가 잘못

저는 인류에 대해

모두가 어떤 의미에서는
초인적이어야만 하는 거죠.

그거 딱 그 컬처 세계관

자기 자신의 노동이나
사고만으로는 기술의 궤적을

근본적으로 바꾸거나 의사결정에

AI가 승인을 구하러 오니
의사결정에 영향을 줄 수는

있겠지만, 그건 제가

내놔서 미래에 진짜 영향을

ko:
저는 과도기가 있을 거라고

장기적으로는 그마저도
아마 사라질 거예요.

지금도 이 방향으로 극단까지
가는 파워리프터들이 있잖아요.

인지의 시대에서
파워리프팅이란 건 뭘까요?

ko:
아마 뭔가를 아는 것 자체로 올림픽을

완벽한 AI 튜터가 있다면 정말

오늘날의 천재들도 인간
정신이 할 수 있는

저도 당신 제품과 가장 잘 맞는

매주 다른 분야를 배워야 하는

예를 들어 많은 사람들은 학교를

뭔가를 배우는 것
자체를 정말 좋아했고요.

ko: 학교에 계속 남아 있고 싶었어요.

박사까지 쭉 남아 있었는데, 더는

대략 말하면, 배우는 것 자체가
좋기도 하지만, 배움이 일종의

힘이 되고 유용하고 생산적인 사람이

그걸 좀 풀어서 짚어보고 싶어요.

모든 사람이 모든 걸 알게
만들지 못한 걸까요?

부담이 너무 크고, 너무

대신 정말 훌륭한 인간 과외
선생님 같은 게 있다면, 동기

부여 측면에서 완전히 다른

학습 자료에서 튕겨져

시간을 쏟았는데 결과가 안

제대로 하면, 배우는
건 기분 좋은 일이에요.

시점엔 아마 AI

누군가에게 코드를 짜보게 해서

수 없는 분야를 얘기하면

그런데 이런 건 상당 부분 제

왜 모두가 어릴 때 물리학을 배워야

초기 교육은 나중에 업계에서 쓸

물리학이 유독 뇌를 가장 잘

모델과 추상화를 세우고,

1차 근사가 있지만 그
뒤에 있을 수도 없을 수도

있는 2차, 3차, 4차

아주 잡음이 많은 시스템을

en: The idea that you're observing a very noisy system, but there are these fundamental frequencies that you can abstract away.

추상화해낼 수 있는 근본적인
주파수들이 있다는 발상이요.

물리학자가 수업에 들어와서
"구형 소를 가정하라"고

하면 다들 웃지만, 사실

업계 전반에 아주 잘

소를 여러 면에서 구로

예를 들어 정말 좋은 책이 있는데,

생물학에 대해 이야기하는

이것도 제가 추천하고

정말 흥미로운 근사들을

동물들의 스케일링 법칙도
그래프로 그릴 수 있어요.

동물을 하나의 부피로
이야기할 수 있어요.

그 열 발산에 대해서도 이야기할
수 있는데, 열 발산은

표면적에 비례해 늘어나고,
표면적은 제곱으로 커지거든요.
en: You can talk about the heat dissipation of that, because your heat dissipation grows as the surface area, which is growing as a square.

ko: 그런데 열 생성량은 세제곱으로 늘어나요.

그래서 물리학자들은 세상의
문제를 풀어내는 데 필요한
en: So I just feel like physicists have all the right cognitive tools to approach problem solving in the world.

인지적 도구를 다 갖추고
있다는 생각이 들어요.

ko:
어떤 시스템이나 대상을
관찰할 때, 제 머릿속에는

뒤엉킨 아이디어와

ko:
그중에서 정말 중요한 게
뭔지 찾으려고 하는 거죠.
